BYLAWS OF SUNRISE COOPERATIVE HOUSING SOCIETY
(As adopted by the Promoter Members on 10.04.2017)

PREAMBLE

Whereas the members of the Sunrise Cooperative Housing Society have agreed to constitute a cooperative housing society for the purpose of providing housing accommodation to its members and for matters connected therewith, the following Bylaws are hereby adopted.

CHAPTER I: NAME, REGISTERED OFFICE AND OBJECTS

1. Name: The name of the society shall be Sunrise Cooperative Housing Society (hereinafter referred to as "the Society"). Sunrise Cooperative Housing Society registered_under Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960. Record status: current.

2. Registered Office: The registered office of the Society shall be situated at Plot No. 27, Sunrise Society Lane, Off. Palm Beach Road, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra 400705, or at such other place as the General Body may decide from time to time.

3. Area of Operation: The area of operation of the Society shall be the Municipal Corporation area of Navi Mumbai.

4. Objects of the Society:
   a) To acquire by purchase, lease, or otherwise, land and buildings for the purpose of providing residential accommodation to its members.
   b) To construct, maintain, and repair buildings and other structures for the benefit of members.
   c) To provide common amenities such as water supply, electricity, sanitation, and other services for the convenience of members.
   d) To borrow funds, with the approval of the General Body, for the purposes of the Society.
   e) To invest funds of the Society in accordance with the provisions of the Act and rules.
   f) To undertake all such other activities as may be necessary for the attainment of the above objects.

CHAPTER II: MEMBERSHIP

5. Eligibility: Any person competent to contract, who is the owner or intending owner of a flat in the building of the Society, shall be eligible for membership. No person shall be admitted as a member except by a resolution passed by the Managing Committee.

6. Admission of Members: Application for membership shall be made in the prescribed form. The Managing Committee shall consider the application and communicate its decision within thirty days of receipt.

7. Rights of Members: Every member shall have the right to:
   a) Vote at General Body meetings.
   b) Hold office in the Society subject to eligibility criteria.
   c) Inspect the books and records of the Society as per the Act.
   d) Receive copies of the audited balance sheet and annual report.

8. Cessation of Membership: Membership shall cease upon transfer of the flat, death (subject to nomination), or expulsion in accordance with the Act.

CHAPTER III: GENERAL BODY MEETINGS

9. Annual General Body Meeting: The Society shall hold its Annual General Body Meeting within six months of the close of the financial year. The agenda shall include:
   a) Confirmation of minutes of the previous meeting.
   b) Presentation of audited accounts and annual report.
   c) Election of the Managing Committee, if due.
   d) Appointment of auditor.
   e) Any other business with the permission of the Chair.
13. Voting: Subject to the provisions of the Act and these bylaws, all questions coming before the General Body shall be decided by a majority of votes of the members present and voting. Voting shall be by show of hands, unless a poll is demanded by not less than one-tenth of the members present. When a poll is demanded, it shall be taken in such manner as the Chairman may direct. Each member shall have one vote only, irrespective of the number of shares held. Voting by proxy shall not be permitted. Voting by postal ballot shall be permitted for such matters as may be specified by the Managing Committee, subject to the provisions of the Act and the rules.

14. Minutes of Meetings: The minutes of the proceedings of every General Body meeting shall be recorded in a minute book maintained for the purpose, and shall be signed by the Chairman of the meeting or by the Chairman of the next succeeding meeting after confirmation. The minutes shall be confirmed at the next meeting and shall be open to inspection by any member during office hours.

15. Power of General Body: The General Body shall have the following powers:
   a) To elect the Managing Committee.
   b) To appoint and remove the auditor.
   c) To approve the annual budget and audited accounts.
   d) To amend the bylaws of the Society.
   e) To approve the sale, mortgage, lease or other disposition of the property of the Society.
   f) To approve any borrowing by the Society.
   g) To consider and decide upon any other matter placed before it by the Managing Committee or requisitioned by members in accordance with the Act.

CHAPTER IV: MANAGING COMMITTEE

The bylaws state that the General Body quorum_required is 30 percent. Record status: current.

16. Constitution of the Managing Committee: The Managing Committee shall consist of not less than five and not more than nine members elected by the General Body from amongst its members. The term of office of the Managing Committee shall be five years. Casual vacancies shall be filled by the Managing Committee, and the member so appointed shall hold office only for the remainder of the term of the member whose place he/she has been appointed to fill.

17. Office Bearers: The Managing Committee shall, at its first meeting after election, elect from amongst its members a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson, a Secretary, a Treasurer and such other office bearers as may be deemed necessary. The office bearers shall hold office as such for a period of one year or for the term of the Managing Committee, whichever is less, and shall be eligible for re-election.

18. Powers and Duties of the Managing Committee: The Managing Committee shall manage the affairs of the Society and shall have the power to:
   a) Admit new members, subject to the provisions of these bylaws.
   b) Maintain the accounts of the Society and present them to the General Body.
   c) Collect and recover all sums due to the Society from members.
   d) Appoint, suspend or remove employees of the Society.
   e) Enter into contracts on behalf of the Society, subject to the approval of the General Body for contracts exceeding the limit prescribed by the Act.
   f) Institute and defend legal proceedings on behalf of the Society.
   g) Do all such other acts and things as may be necessary for the efficient management of the Society, not inconsistent with the Act, the rules, and these bylaws.

19. Meetings of the Managing Committee: The Managing Committee shall meet at least once in every month. The Secretary shall convene a meeting of the Managing Committee at the request of the Chairperson or of not less than one-third of the members of the Committee. The quorum for the meeting of the Managing Committee shall be one-third of the members of the Committee, subject to a minimum of three. Decisions of the Managing Committee shall be by majority of votes of the members present and voting. In case of equality of votes, the Chairperson shall have a casting vote.
BYLAWS OF SUNRISE COOPERATIVE HOUSING SOCIETY

(Registered under the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960)

Registration No. MCS/DR/2017/1142

Date of Registration: 14th March 2017

---

20. Election Procedure

20.1 The election of the Managing Committee shall be held once in every five years, unless the term is extended by the Deputy Registrar under the provisions of the Act. The election shall be conducted in accordance with the rules prescribed under the Act and the bye-laws of the Society.

20.2 The Chief Promoter, or in the case of subsequent elections, the Chairperson of the Managing Committee, shall appoint an Election Officer from amongst the members of the Society, not being a candidate for election, at least sixty days prior to the date fixed for the election.

20.3 The Election Officer shall prepare the final list of voters based on the register of members maintained by the Society, and shall publish the same at least thirty days before the date of election. Any omission or incorrect entry in the list of voters shall be brought to the notice of the Election Officer in writing not later than fifteen days before the date of election, and the Election Officer shall decide the matter within seven days of receipt of such objection. The decision of the Election Officer shall be final.

20.4 Nomination papers shall be filed with the Election Officer in the prescribed form, duly proposed and seconded by members of the Society, not later than fifteen days before the date of election. The scrutiny of nomination papers shall be done on the following day. A member may withdraw his/her candidature within three days of the scrutiny. The final list of contesting candidates shall be published not later than ten days before the date of election.

20.5 Voting shall be by secret ballot. A member who is unable to be present in person may vote by postal ballot, provided such member has applied to the Election Officer in writing at least seven days before the date of election, stating the reason for inability to be present. The postal ballot papers shall be dispatched to such members not later than five days before the date of election, and shall be received back by the Election Officer not later than 5:00 p.m. on the day preceding the date of election.

20.6 The counting of votes shall be done on the day of election or on the next day, in the presence of the candidates or their authorised representatives. The Election Officer shall declare the results and shall hand over the list of elected members to the Secretary of the Society. The results shall be communicated to the Deputy Registrar within fifteen days of the election.

20.7 Any dispute arising out of the election shall be referred to the Deputy Registrar and his/her decision shall be final and binding on the Society.

21. Composition of the Managing Committee

21.1 The Managing Committee shall consist of nine members, of which:

a) Seven members shall be elected from amongst the members of the Society.
   b) One member shall be co-opted from amongst the members of the Society, not being a candidate in the election, to represent the interests of women, scheduled castes, scheduled tribes, or other backward classes, as the case may be.
   c) One member shall be co-opted from amongst the members of the Society to represent the interests of the members belonging to the minority community, if any.

Provided that the co-opted members shall have the right to vote at the meetings of the Managing Committee but shall not have the right to vote at the election of office bearers.

21.2 The term of the Managing Committee shall be five years from the date of election. The term of the co-opted members shall be co-terminus with the term of the Managing Committee.
BYLAWS OF SUNRISE COOPERATIVE HOUSING SOCIETY
(Registered under the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960)
Registration No. MCS/2017/CHS/1842
Registered on 12th June 2017

---

22. FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT

22.1 The financial year of the Society shall be from 1st April to 31st March of the following year.

22.2 The Managing Committee shall cause to be kept proper books of account and such other books as may be required under the Act and the Rules, with respect to:
a) All sums of money received and expended by the Society and the matters in respect of which the receipt and expenditure take place;
b) All sales and purchases of goods and services by the Society;
c) The assets and liabilities of the Society; and
d) All other matters as may be prescribed.

22.3 The books of account and all other records of the Society shall be kept at the registered office of the Society and shall be open to inspection by any member, free of charge, at all reasonable times during business hours, subject to such reasonable restrictions as the Managing Committee may impose, provided that such restrictions shall not be repugnant to the provisions of the Act.

22.4 The Managing Committee shall, within two months from the close of the financial year, prepare the annual accounts of the Society, including the balance sheet and the income and expenditure account, and shall place the same before the General Body at its annual general meeting.

22.5 The accounts of the Society shall be audited annually by an auditor appointed by the General Body. No member of the Managing Committee, and no person who is in the employment of the Society, shall be eligible to be appointed as auditor.

22.6 The auditor shall have access at all times to the books, accounts, and vouchers of the Society, and shall be entitled to require from the office bearers and employees of the Society such information and explanations as may be necessary for the performance of his/her duties.

22.7 The auditor shall report on:
a) The accounts examined by him/her;
b) The balance sheet and the income and expenditure account;
c) Whether, in his/her opinion, the balance sheet and the income and expenditure account give a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the Society as at the end of the financial year;
d) Any irregularities, including any expenditure not authorised by the Act, the Rules, or these Bylaws; and
e) Any other matter which the auditor considers to be relevant to the conduct of the affairs of the Society.

22.8 A copy of the audit report, together with the audited balance sheet and income and expenditure account, shall be forwarded to the Deputy Registrar within fifteen days of the receipt of the report from the auditor.

22.9 The Managing Committee shall place the audit report before the General Body at its next general meeting, and shall also make available a copy thereof to any member on request.

22.10 The Society shall maintain a reserve fund and such other funds as may be required under the Act, the Rules, or these Bylaws. The reserve fund shall not be utilised for any purpose other than that for which it is constituted, except with the prior approval of the General Body and the Deputy Registrar, as required by law.

22.11 No funds of the Society shall be expended for any purpose other than the objects of the Society as set out in these Bylaws, and no portion of the funds of the Society shall be paid by way of bonus, dividend, or profit to any member, except as expressly permitted by the Act.

22.12 The Managing Committee may, with the approval of the General Body, invest the funds of the Society in:
a) A co-operative bank or a scheduled bank;
b) The State Co-operative Bank;
c) Securities of the Central Government or a State Government; or
d) Any other mode of investment permitted by the Act or the Rules.
BYLAWS OF SUNRISE COOPERATIVE HOUSING SOCIETY
(Registered under the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960)
Registration No. BOM/HSG/2017/4567

---

**23. AMENDMENT OF BYLAWS**

23.1 These Bylaws may be amended, added to, or rescinded only by a resolution passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting at a General Body meeting, subject to the provisions of the Act and the Rules.

23.2 Notice of any proposed amendment shall be given in writing to the Secretary at least fifteen days before the date of the General Body meeting at which the amendment is to be considered. The notice shall set out the full text of the proposed amendment.

23.3 The Managing Committee shall include the proposed amendment in the agenda of the General Body meeting and shall circulate the text of the proposed amendment to all members along with the notice of the meeting.

23.4 No amendment shall be effective until it has been registered with the Deputy Registrar in accordance with Section 13 of the Act. The Secretary shall, within thirty days of the passing of the resolution, forward a copy of the resolution and the amended Bylaws to the Deputy Registrar for registration.

23.5 If the Deputy Registrar refuses to register an amendment, the Society may appeal against such refusal in the manner provided by the Act and the Rules.

23.6 Any amendment which is inconsistent with the provisions of the Act, the Rules, or any other law for the time being in force shall be void to the extent of such inconsistency.

---

**24. DISSOLUTION OF THE SOCIETY**

24.1 The Society shall not be dissolved except by an order of the Registrar, or by a resolution passed by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the members present and voting at a General Body meeting specially convened for the purpose, and with the prior approval of the Registrar.

24.2 Upon dissolution, the assets of the Society, after satisfying all debts and liabilities, shall be applied in the following order:
a) Payment of all amounts due to the Society's creditors;
b) Refund of the share capital to members, in proportion to the shares held by them;
c) Distribution of the remaining surplus, if any, among the members in proportion to the amount of their share capital, or in such other manner as may be decided by the General Body and approved by the Registrar.

24.3 The dissolution shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of Sections 102 to 105 of the Act, and the liquidator appointed by the Registrar shall have all the powers conferred by the Act.

24.4 Upon dissolution, the name of the Society shall be struck off the register of societies maintained by the Registrar, and the Society shall cease to exist as a legal entity.

---

**25. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS**

25.1 The Society shall have a common seal, which shall be kept in the custody of the Secretary. The seal shall not be affixed to any document except in the presence of the Secretary and one other member of the Managing Committee, who shall sign the document in token of their presence.

25.2 The Society shall maintain a register of members, a register of shares, a register of transfers, a register of charges, and such other registers and books as may be required under the Act or the Rules. The registers shall be open for inspection by any member at the registered office of the Society during business hours, on payment of the prescribed fee.

25.3 Any notice required to be given to a member under these Bylaws shall be deemed to have been duly given if sent by post, or by electronic mail to the address of the member as recorded in the register of members. The notice shall be deemed to have been served at the time at which the letter or electronic mail would be delivered in the ordinary course of post or transmission.

The committee discussed the quotation at length. Some members felt that the increase was steep and suggested obtaining a comparative quotation from another service provider. However, considering the past service record of M/s. Kothrud Elevators Ltd. and the fact that the lift is now 12 years old, the committee felt that continuity of service was important.

**Decision:** The committee resolved to renew the contract with M/s. Kothrud Elevators Ltd. for one year w.e.f. 1 July 2019 at Rs. 1,20,000/- per annum. The Secretary was authorised to sign the renewal agreement.

**Resolution No. 2019/05/10**

b) **Water Purifier:** The water purifier at the society's borewell is under a maintenance contract with M/s. AquaPure Systems. The contract expires on 31 August 2019. The company has offered a renewal at Rs. 6,500/- per quarter. The committee noted that the purifier has required frequent repairs in the last six months. The Treasurer suggested that the committee review the usage data before renewing. The matter was deferred to the next meeting.
**2. Chairman's Report for the Year 2021-22**

The Chairman read out the Annual Report. Key points:

- **Financial Position:** The society has a surplus of Rs. 4,85,000/- for the year ended 31 March 2022. The reserve fund stands at Rs. 18,20,000/-.
- **Repairs and Maintenance:** Major waterproofing of the terrace of Wing A was completed in December 2021 at a cost of Rs. 2,40,000/-. The lift modernisation project is still pending and will be discussed under a separate agenda item.
- **Compliance:** The society has filed all statutory returns, including GST and TDS, on time. The annual accounts for 2021-22 have been audited.

The Chairman invited questions. A member, Mr. P. V. Kulkarni (Flat No. B-302), asked about the delay in the lift modernisation. The Chairman explained that the committee had received two quotations and was awaiting a third. The matter would be put to vote later in the meeting.

|---|---|

| **Net Surplus** | **4,85,000** |

The Auditor, Mrs. S. R. Iyer, read out the audit report. She noted that the accounts give a true and fair view of the society's affairs. No qualifications were raised.

**Discussion:** A member, Mrs. N. S. Godbole (Flat No. A-101), enquired about the increase in the salary bill. The Treasurer explained that the increase is due to the annual increment and the appointment of a part-time helper in November 2021.

**Resolution No. AGM/2022/01:** The audited accounts for the year ending 31 March 2022 be and are hereby approved and adopted.

The resolution was put to vote and passed unanimously.

**4. Appointment of Auditor for the Year 2022-23**

The term of M/s. Iyer & Associates expires at the end of this meeting. The Chairman proposed the reappointment of the same firm for the year 2022-23 at a remuneration of Rs. 15,000/-.

**Resolution No. AGM/2022/02:** M/s. Iyer & Associates be and are hereby reappointed as the statutory auditors of the society for the financial year 2022-23 at a remuneration of Rs. 15,000/-.

The resolution was passed with 70 votes in favour, 2 abstentions, and 1 against.

**5. Lift Modernisation – Quotations and Decision**

The Chairman placed before the house the status of the lift modernisation project. The lift has been in service for 15 years and has had frequent breakdowns. The committee had obtained quotations from three vendors:

a) **M/s. Kothrud Elevators Ltd.** – Rs. 8,50,000/- (complete modernisation, including new controller, motor, and cab)
b) **M/s. Pune Lift Services** – Rs. 7,90,000/- (similar scope)
c) **M/s. Modern Lifts India** – Rs. 9,20,000/- (premium package with 5-year warranty)

The Chairman noted that the committee had shortlisted M/s. Pune Lift Services on the basis of cost. However, two committee members expressed a preference for M/s. Kothrud Elevators Ltd. due to their long association with the society and their past service record.

**Discussion:** A lengthy discussion followed. Mr. P. V. Kulkarni (B-302) spoke in favour of M/s. Kothrud Elevators Ltd., stating that their existing maintenance contract had been trouble-free. Mrs. S. R. Iyer, the Auditor, pointed out that the difference of Rs. 60,000/- between the two quotes could be covered by the reserve fund without any difficulty. Another member, Mr. R. D. Mehta (C-201), moved that the committee be authorised to negotiate with both vendors and finalise the vendor at the lowest possible cost, subject to a maximum of Rs. 8,50,000/-.
**MANAGING COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES – 28/09/2022 (Continued)**

The Chairman then took up the agenda item on the formation of the Parking Sub-Committee and the Water Tank Maintenance Sub-Committee. It was recalled that at the General Body Meeting held on 18/09/2022, the members had authorised the Managing Committee to constitute these sub-committees and to bring back their recommendations for approval. The Chairman informed the house that the committee had since then constituted both sub-committees and that their reports were now ready for consideration.

**6. Parking Sub-Committee – Constitution and Recommendations**

The Chairman read out the names of the members appointed to the Parking Sub-Committee:

| Mr. S. B. Patil | D-301 | Member |

The sub-committee had been asked to examine the long-standing issue of visitor parking and the unauthorised use of reserved bays. The Chairman summarised the main recommendations of the sub-committee as follows:

a) That the existing 12 visitor parking slots be clearly demarcated with painted lines and signage, and that a register be maintained at the security gate for recording vehicle entry and exit times.

b) That two additional visitor slots be created by converting the unused space near the rear compound wall, adjacent to the garbage room. This would require removal of an old tree stump and levelling of the ground.

c) That the practice of allotting permanent reserved bays to individual flat owners be discontinued with effect from 1st April 2023. Instead, all residents would be required to park in unmarked bays on a first-come-first-served basis. The only exceptions would be the two bays reserved for the Chairman and the Secretary, and one bay reserved for the society's ambulance.

d) That a fine of Rs. 200/- be levied on any vehicle found parked in a visitor slot beyond the permitted 4-hour limit, and that repeat offenders be reported to the Managing Committee for further action.

e) That the society consider engaging a part-time parking attendant during peak hours (6 PM to 10 PM) at a monthly cost of approximately Rs. 3,000/-.

**Discussion:** A lively discussion followed. Mr. P. V. Kulkarni (B-302) said that the proposal to abolish reserved bays would be unpopular with some senior residents who had been allotted specific bays many years ago. He suggested that existing allotments be allowed to continue for the current senior citizens, and that the new rule apply only to new allotments. Mrs. S. R. Iyer, the Auditor, pointed out that the society's parking area had not been formally divided into demarcated bays at the time of registration, and that the allotment of bays had been done informally by successive committees. She opined that this had led to disputes and that a uniform policy was long overdue.

Mr. R. D. Mehta (C-201) asked whether the sub-committee had studied the actual number of vehicles owned by residents as against the total parking capacity. The Convenor, Mrs. Deshpande, replied that the sub-committee had conducted a survey in the first week of October and found that there were 78 two-wheelers and 54 cars registered to residents, against a total capacity of 96 car spaces and 60 two-wheeler spaces. She admitted that the survey had been done informally through the security staff and that some residents had not responded.

The tenders had been invited in August 2021, and the last date for submission was 30th September 2021. The following bids were received:

Mr. Nair noted that Skyline Lifts had quoted the lowest amount, but had not previously serviced lifts of this make (KONE model). Kothari Elevators had serviced the lifts for the past three years and had a good record of response time, including two emergency call-outs in July 2021. Reliable Elevators had submitted their bid by hand on 1st October, one day after the deadline, and the Sub-Committee had decided to include it for comparison only, not for award.

**Discussion:** Mrs. S. R. Iyer, the Auditor, asked whether the Sub-Committee had verified the credentials of Skyline Lifts. Mr. Nair replied that they had obtained two references from other societies in the area, but had not visited any of those sites. She further pointed out that the difference between the lowest and second-lowest bid was about Rs. 8,400, which was not substantial, and that the track record of the existing provider should be given weight.

Mr. R. D. Mehta (C-201) said that the society should not always favour the incumbent, and that a new provider should be given a chance at least once. He noted that the lift breakdown in August had inconvenienced the elderly residents on the upper floors.

**Resolution No. MC/2021/22:** The Managing Committee resolved to award the AMC for the two lifts to Kothari Elevators Pvt. Ltd. for a period of one year from 1st December 2021 to 30th November 2022 at a cost of Rs. 48,000/- per annum, subject to the following conditions:
a) The contractor shall provide a 24-hour emergency call-out facility.
b) The contractor shall maintain a service log book at the society office, to be signed by the Secretary after each visit.
c) The contract may be terminated by either party with one month's notice.

The Committee noted that the decision was taken by a majority of 5 votes in favour and 2 against. Mr. Mehta and Mrs. Iyer recorded their dissent, with Mr. Mehta stating that he would raise the matter at the next General Body meeting.

**Item 6: Compliance with the Deputy Registrar's Order dated 22nd October 2021**

The Secretary, Mrs. Deshpande, read out the salient features of the order received from the Office of the Deputy Registrar, Co-operative Societies, Pune, in response to the society's application for approval of the revised bye-laws. The order had directed the society to:
a) Re-submit the draft bye-laws with the deletion of Bye-law No. 14(iv) regarding the levy of a special charge on non-resident owners.
b) Clarify the provision regarding the composition of the Managing Committee, specifically whether the post of the Treasurer could be held by the same person as the Secretary.
c) Submit the audited accounts for the years 2018-19 and 2019-20, which had not been filed with the office.

The Secretary informed the Committee that the draft bye-laws had been prepared by the legal advisor, and that the deletion of Bye-law No. 14(iv) had been noted. However, she sought the Committee's guidance on the other two points.

**Item 1: Confirmation of Minutes of the previous meeting**

The minutes of the Managing Committee Meeting No. 11/2021-22 held on 28th October 2021 were read out. Mr. Patil suggested a minor correction to the wording of Resolution No. MC/2021/20 regarding the water tank cleaning schedule. The correction was accepted and the minutes were confirmed with the said amendment.

**Item 2: Presentation of the Structural Audit Report**

Mr. D. Kulkarni, the structural engineer, presented the findings of the structural audit conducted on 2nd and 3rd November 2021. He circulated a detailed report (copy kept in the society office for inspection by members). The key findings are summarised below:

1. **Exterior walls:** Cracks observed on the southern elevation of the building, primarily on the ground and first floors. These appear to be due to thermal movement and minor settlement. The cracks are not structurally significant at present but require monitoring and sealing.

2. **Balconies:** The concrete on the edge of the balconies on the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th floors is spalling in several places. The reinforcement bars are exposed and rusted. This is a common issue in buildings of this age (constructed 1998) and needs immediate attention to prevent further deterioration.

3. **Water seepage:** Seepage is reported from the terrace and around the overhead water tank area. The water-proofing layer on the terrace has failed in patches. This is causing dampness on the ceiling of the 4th floor flats.

4. **Staircase:** The handrails on the staircase are loose at certain points and need re-fixing. The anti-skid treads on the steps are worn out and a few are broken.

5. **Lift machine room:** The floor of the lift machine room has minor cracks. The room is otherwise in a satisfactory condition.

Mr. Kulkarni clarified that the building is structurally sound overall, and no major structural repairs are required at this stage. He recommended a course of preventive and corrective maintenance as detailed in his written report.

---

**Item 3: Discussion on Repair Proposals and Estimates**

The Committee discussed the audit findings in detail. The Secretary, Mrs. Deshpande, had obtained estimates from three contractors for the proposed works. The estimates were for the following work items:

a) Sealing of cracks on exterior walls – Rs. 45,000/-
b) Repair of balcony edges, including chipping of loose concrete, rust removal, and re-plastering – Rs. 1,20,000/-
c) Re-waterproofing of the terrace and tank area – Rs. 85,000/-
d) Repair and re-fixing of staircase handrails and replacement of anti-skid treads – Rs. 30,000/-
e) Repair of lift machine room floor – Rs. 15,000/-

The total estimated cost for all items was approximately Rs. 2,95,000/-.

The Committee noted that the estimates were on the higher side, and Mr. Mehta suggested that the work of balcony repairs be done in phases, starting with the most affected balconies on the 4th floor. Mrs. Iyer, the Treasurer, expressed concern about the immediate availability of funds. She stated that the society's fixed deposit of Rs. 3,00,000/- was maturing in December 2021, and a portion of it could be used for these repairs. However, she cautioned against exhausting the entire deposit, as a contingency fund was necessary.

**Members Present:**
1. Mr. R. Kulkarni – Chairman
2. Mrs. S. Deshpande – Secretary
3. Mrs. P. Iyer – Treasurer
4. Mr. A. Mehta – Member

7. Mrs. N. Kulkarni – Member

**In Attendance:**
Mr. D. Kelkar, Advocate, Legal Advisor

**Absent:**
None

**Item 1: Confirmation of Minutes of the Previous Meeting**

The minutes of the Managing Committee meeting held on 9th April 2023 were read out. The minutes were confirmed by the members present. There were no amendments proposed.

---

**Item 2: Legal Opinion on Structural Audit and Repair Liability**

The Chairman placed before the Committee the legal opinion obtained from our Legal Advisor, Adv. D. Kelkar, regarding the liability for the cost of major repairs and the procedure to be followed for the same.

The Committee had sought the opinion in view of the structural audit report and the proposed repair works. The opinion, dated 2nd May 2023, was read out in detail. The key points of the opinion are summarised below:

a) **Liability for Repairs:** As per the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960 and the Model Bye-laws, the cost of repairs to the common areas and the external structure of the building is the responsibility of all members of the society. This includes repairs to the terrace, external walls, staircase, and lift machine room. The society is empowered to raise the necessary funds through a special contribution or by utilising the society's reserves.

b) **Procedure for Raising Funds:** The opinion stated that for any repair work exceeding a specified limit, a resolution must be passed in the General Body Meeting. The opinion referred to Bye-law No. 71, which requires a special resolution for major repairs. The exact wording of the opinion was noted: "The Managing Committee is authorised to undertake the repairs and to levy a special contribution from members, provided a clear majority of the members present and voting at a General Body Meeting pass a resolution to this effect. The members must be given at least 14 days' notice of the meeting, along with the details of the proposed expenditure and the mode of recovery."

c) **Recovery of Contribution:** Adv. Kelkar clarified that the special contribution, once sanctioned by the General Body, becomes a debt due to the society. The society can recover the amount as arrears of maintenance charges, and the same can be included in the property tax bill or recovered through legal proceedings if necessary.

d) **Utilisation of Reserve Fund:** The opinion noted that the society's reserve fund, including the Fixed Deposit maturing in December 2021, can be utilised for the repairs. However, the opinion cautioned that the society should maintain a minimum contingency fund as per the bye-laws, which is typically 25% of the annual maintenance budget. The opinion stated that the society may utilise up to 75% of the reserve fund for major repairs without seeking prior approval from the Deputy Registrar, but any utilisation beyond this limit would require the Registrar's permission.

The Committee discussed the opinion at length. The Chairman noted that the opinion was clear on the procedure. Mr. Mehta expressed a view that the society should first exhaust the reserve fund before levying a special contribution on members. He argued that many members, especially the elderly, would find it difficult to pay a large lump sum amount. Mrs. Iyer, the Treasurer, pointed out that the reserve fund, including the fixed deposit of Rs. 3,00,000/- which had matured, was only about Rs. 4,50,000/- in total. The estimated cost of repairs was around Rs. 2,95,000/-. If the entire repair cost was met from the reserve fund, the society would be left with only about Rs. 1,55,000/-, which was below the recommended contingency level.

BYLAWS OF SUNRISE COOPERATIVE HOUSING SOCIETY
(As adopted by the Promoter Members on 10.04.2017)

PREAMBLE

Whereas the members of the Sunrise Cooperative Housing Society have agreed to constitute a cooperative housing society for the purpose of providing housing accommodation to its members and for matters connected therewith, the following Bylaws are hereby adopted.

CHAPTER I: NAME, REGISTERED OFFICE AND OBJECTS

1. Name: The name of the society shall be Sunrise Cooperative Housing Society (hereinafter referred to as "the Society"). Sunrise Cooperative Housing Society registered_under Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960. Record status: current.

2. Registered Office: The registered office of the Society shall be situated at Plot No. 27, Sunrise Society Lane, Off. Palm Beach Road, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra 400705, or at such other place as the General Body may decide from time to time.

3. Area of Operation: The area of operation of the Society shall be the Municipal Corporation area of Navi Mumbai.

4. Objects of the Society:
   a) To acquire by purchase, lease, or otherwise, land and buildings for the purpose of providing residential accommodation to its members.
   b) To construct, maintain, and repair buildings and other structures for the benefit of members.
   c) To provide common amenities such as water supply, electricity, sanitation, and other services for the convenience of members.
   d) To borrow funds, with the approval of the General Body, for the purposes of the Society.
   e) To invest funds of the Society in accordance with the provisions of the Act and rules.
   f) To undertake all such other activities as may be necessary for the attainment of the above objects.

CHAPTER II: MEMBERSHIP

5. Eligibility: Any person competent to contract, who is the owner or intending owner of a flat in the building of the Society, shall be eligible for membership. No person shall be admitted as a member except by a resolution passed by the Managing Committee.

6. Admission of Members: Application for membership shall be made in the prescribed form. The Managing Committee shall consider the application and communicate its decision within thirty days of receipt.

7. Rights of Members: Every member shall have the right to:
   a) Vote at General Body meetings.
   b) Hold office in the Society subject to eligibility criteria.
   c) Inspect the books and records of the Society as per the Act.
   d) Receive copies of the audited balance sheet and annual report.

8. Cessation of Membership: Membership shall cease upon transfer of the flat, death (subject to nomination), or expulsion in accordance with the Act.

CHAPTER III: GENERAL BODY MEETINGS

9. Annual General Body Meeting: The Society shall hold its Annual General Body Meeting within six months of the close of the financial year. The agenda shall include:
   a) Confirmation of minutes of the previous meeting.
   b) Presentation of audited accounts and annual report.
   c) Election of the Managing Committee, if due.
   d) Appointment of auditor.
   e) Any other business with the permission of the Chair.

13. Voting: Subject to the provisions of the Act and these bylaws, all questions coming before the General Body shall be decided by a majority of votes of the members present and voting. Voting shall be by show of hands, unless a poll is demanded by not less than one-tenth of the members present. When a poll is demanded, it shall be taken in such manner as the Chairman may direct. Each member shall have one vote only, irrespective of the number of shares held. Voting by proxy shall not be permitted. Minutes of Meetings: The minutes of the proceedings of every General Body meeting shall be recorded in a minute book maintained for the purpose, and shall be signed by the Chairman of the meeting or by the Chairman of the next succeeding meeting after confirmation. The minutes shall be confirmed at the next meeting and shall be open to inspection by any member during office hours.

15. Power of General Body: The General Body shall have the following powers:
   a) To elect the Managing Committee.
   b) To appoint and remove the auditor.
   c) To approve the annual budget and audited accounts.
   d) To amend the bylaws of the Society.
   e) To approve the sale, mortgage, lease or other disposition of the property of the Society.
   f) To approve any borrowing by the Society.

CHAPTER IV: MANAGING COMMITTEE

The bylaws state that the General Body quorum_required is 30 percent. Record status: current.

16. Constitution of the Managing Committee: The Managing Committee shall consist of not less than five and not more than nine members elected by the General Body from amongst its members. The term of office of the Managing Committee shall be five years. Casual vacancies shall be filled by the Managing Committee, and the member so appointed shall hold office only for the remainder of the term of the member whose place he/she has been appointed to fill.

17. Office Bearers: The Managing Committee shall, at its first meeting after election, elect from amongst its members a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson, a Secretary, a Treasurer and such other office bearers as may be deemed necessary. The office bearers shall hold office as such for a period of one year or for the term of the Managing Committee, whichever is less, and shall be eligible for re-election.

18. Powers and Duties of the Managing Committee: The Managing Committee shall manage the affairs of the Society and shall have the power to:
   a) Admit new members, subject to the provisions of these bylaws.
   b) Maintain the accounts of the Society and present them to the General Body.
   c) Collect and recover all sums due to the Society from members.
   d) Appoint, suspend or remove employees of the Society.
   e) Enter into contracts on behalf of the Society, subject to the approval of the General Body for contracts exceeding the limit prescribed by the Act.
   f) Institute and defend legal proceedings on behalf of the Society.
   g) Do all such other acts and things as may be necessary for the efficient management of the Society, not inconsistent with the Act, the rules, and these bylaws.

19. Meetings of the Managing Committee: The Managing Committee shall meet at least once in every month. The Secretary shall convene a meeting of the Managing Committee at the request of the Chairperson or of not less than one-third of the members of the Committee. The quorum for the meeting of the Managing Committee shall be one-third of the members of the Committee, subject to a minimum of three. Decisions of the Managing Committee shall be by majority of votes of the members present and voting. In case of equality of votes, the Chairperson shall have a casting vote.

20. Election Procedure

20.1 The election of the Managing Committee shall be held once in every five years, unless the term is extended by the Deputy Registrar under the provisions of the Act. The election shall be conducted in accordance with the rules prescribed under the Act and the bye-laws of the Society.

20.2 The Chief Promoter, or in the case of subsequent elections, the Chairperson of the Managing Committee, shall appoint an Election Officer from amongst the members of the Society, not being a candidate for election, at least sixty days prior to the date fixed for the election.

20.3 The Election Officer shall prepare the final list of voters based on the register of members maintained by the Society, and shall publish the same at least thirty days before the date of election. Any omission or incorrect entry in the list of voters shall be brought to the notice of the Election Officer in writing not later than fifteen days before the date of election, and the Election Officer shall decide the matter within seven days of receipt of such objection. The decision of the Election Officer shall be final.

20.4 Nomination papers shall be filed with the Election Officer in the prescribed form, duly proposed and seconded by members of the Society, not later than fifteen days before the date of election. The scrutiny of nomination papers shall be done on the following day. A member may withdraw his/her candidature within three days of the scrutiny. The final list of contesting candidates shall be published not later than ten days before the date of election.

20.5 Voting shall be by secret ballot. A member who is unable to be present in person may vote by postal ballot, provided such member has applied to the Election Officer in writing at least seven days before the date of election, stating the reason for inability to be present. The postal ballot papers shall be dispatched to such members not later than five days before the date of election, and shall be received back by the Election Officer not later than 5:00 p.m. on the day preceding the date of election.

20.6 The counting of votes shall be done on the day of election or on the next day, in the presence of the candidates or their authorised representatives. The Election Officer shall declare the results and shall hand over the list of elected members to the Secretary of the Society. The results shall be communicated to the Deputy Registrar within fifteen days of the election.

20.7 Any dispute arising out of the election shall be referred to the Deputy Registrar and his/her decision shall be final and binding on the Society.

21. Composition of the Managing Committee

21.1 The Managing Committee shall consist of nine members, of which:

a) Seven members shall be elected from amongst the members of the Society.
   b) One member shall be co-opted from amongst the members of the Society, not being a candidate in the election, to represent the interests of women, scheduled castes, scheduled tribes, or other backward classes, as the case may be.
   c) One member shall be co-opted from amongst the members of the Society to represent the interests of the members belonging to the minority community, if any.

Provided that the co-opted members shall have the right to vote at the meetings of the Managing Committee but shall not have the right to vote at the election of office bearers.

21.2 The term of the Managing Committee shall be five years from the date of election. The term of the co-opted members shall be co-terminus with the term of the Managing Committee.

22.2 The Managing Committee shall cause to be kept proper books of account and such other books as may be required under the Act and the Rules, with respect to:
a) All sums of money received and expended by the Society and the matters in respect of which the receipt and expenditure take place;
b) All sales and purchases of goods and services by the Society;
c) The assets and liabilities of the Society; and
d) All other matters as may be prescribed.

22.3 The books of account and all other records of the Society shall be kept at the registered office of the Society and shall be open to inspection by any member, free of charge, at all reasonable times during business hours, subject to such reasonable restrictions as the Managing Committee may impose, provided that such restrictions shall not be repugnant to the provisions of the Act.

22.4 The Managing Committee shall, within two months from the close of the financial year, prepare the annual accounts of the Society, including the balance sheet and the income and expenditure account, and shall place the same before the General Body at its annual general meeting.

22.5 The accounts of the Society shall be audited annually by an auditor appointed by the General Body. No member of the Managing Committee, and no person who is in the employment of the Society, shall be eligible to be appointed as auditor.

22.6 The auditor shall have access at all times to the books, accounts, and vouchers of the Society, and shall be entitled to require from the office bearers and employees of the Society such information and explanations as may be necessary for the performance of his/her duties.

22.7 The auditor shall report on:
a) The accounts examined by him/her;
b) The balance sheet and the income and expenditure account;
c) Whether, in his/her opinion, the balance sheet and the income and expenditure account give a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the Society as at the end of the financial year;
d) Any irregularities, including any expenditure not authorised by the Act, the Rules, or these Bylaws; and
e) Any other matter which the auditor considers to be relevant to the conduct of the affairs of the Society.

22.8 A copy of the audit report, together with the audited balance sheet and income and expenditure account, shall be forwarded to the Deputy Registrar within fifteen days of the receipt of the report from the auditor.

22.9 The Managing Committee shall place the audit report before the General Body at its next general meeting, and shall also make available a copy thereof to any member on request.

22.10 The Society shall maintain a reserve fund and such other funds as may be required under the Act, the Rules, or these Bylaws. The reserve fund shall not be utilised for any purpose other than that for which it is constituted, except with the prior approval of the General Body and the Deputy Registrar, as required by law.

22.11 No funds of the Society shall be expended for any purpose other than the objects of the Society as set out in these Bylaws, and no portion of the funds of the Society shall be paid by way of bonus, dividend, or profit to any member, except as expressly permitted by the Act.

22.12 The Managing Committee may, with the approval of the General Body, invest the funds of the Society in:
a) A co-operative bank or a scheduled bank;
b) The State Co-operative Bank;
c) Securities of the Central Government or a State Government; or
d) Any other mode of investment permitted by the Act or the Rules.

**23. AMENDMENT OF BYLAWS**

23.1 These Bylaws may be amended, added to, or rescinded only by a resolution passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting at a General Body meeting, subject to the provisions of the Act and the Rules.

23.2 Notice of any proposed amendment shall be given in writing to the Secretary at least fifteen days before the date of the General Body meeting at which the amendment is to be considered. The notice shall set out the full text of the proposed amendment.

23.3 The Managing Committee shall include the proposed amendment in the agenda of the General Body meeting and shall circulate the text of the proposed amendment to all members along with the notice of the meeting.

23.4 No amendment shall be effective until it has been registered with the Deputy Registrar in accordance with Section 13 of the Act. The Secretary shall, within thirty days of the passing of the resolution, forward a copy of the resolution and the amended Bylaws to the Deputy Registrar for registration.

23.5 If the Deputy Registrar refuses to register an amendment, the Society may appeal against such refusal in the manner provided by the Act and the Rules.

23.6 Any amendment which is inconsistent with the provisions of the Act, the Rules, or any other law for the time being in force shall be void to the extent of such inconsistency.

---

**24. DISSOLUTION OF THE SOCIETY**

24.1 The Society shall not be dissolved except by an order of the Registrar, or by a resolution passed by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the members present and voting at a General Body meeting specially convened for the purpose, and with the prior approval of the Registrar.

24.2 Upon dissolution, the assets of the Society, after satisfying all debts and liabilities, shall be applied in the following order:
a) Payment of all amounts due to the Society's creditors;
b) Refund of the share capital to members, in proportion to the shares held by them;
c) Distribution of the remaining surplus, if any, among the members in proportion to the amount of their share capital, or in such other manner as may be decided by the General Body and approved by the Registrar.

24.3 The dissolution shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of Sections 102 to 105 of the Act, and the liquidator appointed by the Registrar shall have all the powers conferred by the Act.

24.4 Upon dissolution, the name of the Society shall be struck off the register of societies maintained by the Registrar, and the Society shall cease to exist as a legal entity.

---

**25. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS**

25.1 The Society shall have a common seal, which shall be kept in the custody of the Secretary. The seal shall not be affixed to any document except in the presence of the Secretary and one other member of the Managing Committee, who shall sign the document in token of their presence.

25.2 The Society shall maintain a register of members, a register of shares, a register of transfers, a register of charges, and such other registers and books as may be required under the Act or the Rules. The registers shall be open for inspection by any member at the registered office of the Society during business hours, on payment of the prescribed fee.

25.3 Any notice required to be given to a member under these Bylaws shall be deemed to have been duly given if sent by post, or by electronic mail to the address of the member as recorded in the register of members. The notice shall be deemed to have been served at the time at which the letter or electronic mail would be delivered in the ordinary course of post or transmission.

The sub-committee had been asked to examine the long-standing issue of visitor parking and the unauthorised use of reserved bays. The Chairman summarised the main recommendations of the sub-committee as follows:

b) That two additional visitor slots be created by converting the unused space near the rear compound wall, adjacent to the garbage room. This would require removal of an old tree stump and levelling of the ground.

**Item 5: Tender for Annual Maintenance Contract (AMC) for Lift Servicing**

The Convenor of the Tender Sub-Committee, Mr. S. R. Nair (A-101), placed the comparative statement of the three tenders received for the AMC of the society's two lifts. The tenders had been invited in August 2021, and the last date for submission was 30th September 2021. The following bids were received:

| Sr. No. | Name of Firm | Quoted Annual Amount (Rs.) | Remarks |
|---------|--------------|----------------------------|---------|
| 1 | Kothari Elevators Pvt. Ltd. | 48,000 | Existing service provider |
| 2 | Skyline Lifts & Services | 39,600 | New bidder |
| 3 | Reliable Elevators Co. | 45,000 | Bid received late, considered |

Mr. Nair noted that Skyline Lifts had quoted the lowest amount, but had not previously serviced lifts of this make (KONE model). Kothari Elevators had serviced the lifts for the past three years and had a good record of response time, including two emergency call-outs in July 2021. Reliable Elevators had submitted their bid by hand on 1st October, one day after the deadline, and the Sub-Committee had decided to include it for comparison only, not for award.

**Discussion:** Mrs. S. R. Iyer, the Auditor, asked whether the Sub-Committee had verified the credentials of Skyline Lifts. Mr. Nair replied that they had obtained two references from other societies in the area, but had not visited any of those sites. She further pointed out that the difference between the lowest and second-lowest bid was about Rs. 8,400, which was not substantial, and that the track record of the existing provider should be given weight.

Mr. R. D. Mehta (C-201) said that the society should not always favour the incumbent, and that a new provider should be given a chance at least once. He noted that the lift breakdown in August had inconvenienced the elderly residents on the upper floors.

**Resolution No. MC/2021/22:** The Managing Committee resolved to award the AMC for the two lifts to Kothari Elevators Pvt. Ltd. for a period of one year from 1st December 2021 to 30th November 2022 at a cost of Rs. 48,000/- per annum, subject to the following conditions:
a) The contractor shall provide a 24-hour emergency call-out facility.
b) The contractor shall maintain a service log book at the society office, to be signed by the Secretary after each visit.
c) The contract may be terminated by either party with one month's notice.

The Committee noted that the decision was taken by a majority of 5 votes in favour and 2 against. Mr. Mehta and Mrs. Iyer recorded their dissent, with Mr. Mehta stating that he would raise the matter at the next General Body meeting.

b) Clarify the provision regarding the composition of the Managing Committee, specifically whether the post of the Treasurer could be held by the same person as the Secretary.
c) Submit the audited accounts for the years 2018-19 and 2019-20, which had not been filed with the office.

The Secretary informed the Committee that the draft bye-laws had been prepared by the legal advisor, and that the deletion of Bye-law No. 14(iv) had been noted. However, she sought the Committee's guidance on the other two points.

Present: Mrs. S. Deshpande (Secretary), Mr. R. Mehta (Chairman), Mrs. A. Iyer (Treasurer), Mr. V. Kulkarni, Mrs. P. Joshi, Mr. S. Patil, Mr. N. Rao

Absent: None.

In attendance: Mr. D. Kulkarni (Structural Engineer, M/s. D. Kulkarni & Associates), Mr. F. D'Souza (Auditor, M/s. D'Souza & Co.)

---

**Item 1: Confirmation of Minutes of the previous meeting**

The minutes of the Managing Committee Meeting No. 11/2021-22 held on 28th October 2021 were read out. Mr. Patil suggested a minor correction to the wording of Resolution No. MC/2021/20 regarding the water tank cleaning schedule. The correction was accepted and the minutes were confirmed with the said amendment.

---

**Item 2: Presentation of the Structural Audit Report**

Mr. D. Kulkarni, the structural engineer, presented the findings of the structural audit conducted on 2nd and 3rd November 2021. He circulated a detailed report (copy kept in the society office for inspection by members). The key findings are summarised below:

1. **Exterior walls:** Cracks observed on the southern elevation of the building, primarily on the ground and first floors. These appear to be due to thermal movement and minor settlement. The cracks are not structurally significant at present but require monitoring and sealing.

2. **Balconies:** The concrete on the edge of the balconies on the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th floors is spalling in several places. The reinforcement bars are exposed and rusted. This is a common issue in buildings of this age (constructed 1998) and needs immediate attention to prevent further deterioration.

3. **Water seepage:** Seepage is reported from the terrace and around the overhead water tank area. The water-proofing layer on the terrace has failed in patches. This is causing dampness on the ceiling of the 4th floor flats.

4. **Staircase:** The handrails on the staircase are loose at certain points and need re-fixing. The anti-skid treads on the steps are worn out and a few are broken.

5. **Lift machine room:** The floor of the lift machine room has minor cracks. The room is otherwise in a satisfactory condition.

Mr. Kulkarni clarified that the building is structurally sound overall, and no major structural repairs are required at this stage. He recommended a course of preventive and corrective maintenance as detailed in his written report.

---

**Item 3: Discussion on Repair Proposals and Estimates**

The Committee discussed the audit findings in detail. The Secretary, Mrs. Deshpande, had obtained estimates from three contractors for the proposed works. The estimates were for the following work items:

a) Sealing of cracks on exterior walls – Rs. 45,000/-
b) Repair of balcony edges, including chipping of loose concrete, rust removal, and re-plastering – Rs. 1,20,000/-
c) Re-waterproofing of the terrace and tank area – Rs. 85,000/-
d) Repair and re-fixing of staircase handrails and replacement of anti-skid treads – Rs. 30,000/-
e) Repair of lift machine room floor – Rs. 15,000/-

The total estimated cost for all items was approximately Rs. 2,95,000/-.

The Committee noted that the estimates were on the higher side, and Mr. Mehta suggested that the work of balcony repairs be done in phases, starting with the most affected balconies on the 4th floor. Mrs. Iyer, the Treasurer, expressed concern about the immediate availability of funds. She stated that the society's fixed deposit of Rs. 3,00,000/- was maturing in December 2021, and a portion of it could be used for these repairs. However, she cautioned against exhausting the entire deposit, as a contingency fund was necessary.

**Item 1: Confirmation of Minutes of the Previous Meeting**

The minutes of the Managing Committee meeting held on 9th April 2023 were read out. The minutes were confirmed by the members present. There were no amendments proposed.

---

**Item 2: Legal Opinion on Structural Audit and Repair Liability**

The Chairman placed before the Committee the legal opinion obtained from our Legal Advisor, Adv. D. Kelkar, regarding the liability for the cost of major repairs and the procedure to be followed for the same.

The Committee had sought the opinion in view of the structural audit report and the proposed repair works. The opinion, dated 2nd May 2023, was read out in detail. The key points of the opinion are summarised below:

a) **Liability for Repairs:** As per the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960 and the Model Bye-laws, the cost of repairs to the common areas and the external structure of the building is the responsibility of all members of the society. This includes repairs to the terrace, external walls, staircase, and lift machine room. The society is empowered to raise the necessary funds through a special contribution or by utilising the society's reserves.

b) **Procedure for Raising Funds:** The opinion stated that for any repair work exceeding a specified limit, a resolution must be passed in the General Body Meeting. The opinion referred to Bye-law No. 71, which requires a special resolution for major repairs. The exact wording of the opinion was noted: "The Managing Committee is authorised to undertake the repairs and to levy a special contribution from members, provided a clear majority of the members present and voting at a General Body Meeting pass a resolution to this effect. The members must be given at least 14 days' notice of the meeting, along with the details of the proposed expenditure and the mode of recovery."

c) **Recovery of Contribution:** Adv. Kelkar clarified that the special contribution, once sanctioned by the General Body, becomes a debt due to the society. The society can recover the amount as arrears of maintenance charges, and the same can be included in the property tax bill or recovered through legal proceedings if necessary.

d) **Utilisation of Reserve Fund:** The opinion noted that the society's reserve fund, including the Fixed Deposit maturing in December 2021, can be utilised for the repairs. However, the opinion cautioned that the society should maintain a minimum contingency fund as per the bye-laws, which is typically 25% of the annual maintenance budget. The opinion stated that the society may utilise up to 75% of the reserve fund for major repairs without seeking prior approval from the Deputy Registrar, but any utilisation beyond this limit would require the Registrar's permission.

The Committee discussed the opinion at length. The Chairman noted that the opinion was clear on the procedure. Mr. Mehta expressed a view that the society should first exhaust the reserve fund before levying a special contribution on members. He argued that many members, especially the elderly, would find it difficult to pay a large lump sum amount. Mrs. Iyer, the Treasurer, pointed out that the reserve fund, including the fixed deposit of Rs. 3,00,000/- which had matured, was only about Rs. 4,50,000/- in total. The estimated cost of repairs was around Rs. 2,95,000/-. If the entire repair cost was met from the reserve fund, the society would be left with only about Rs. 1,55,000/-, which was below the recommended contingency level.
